key_insight: A compact vision–language approach plus a new benchmark enables small models to accurately detect time‑series anomalies and provide grounded, human‑readable rationales, offering trusted, efficient anomaly reasoning.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between powerful VLMs and sequential anomaly detection by addressing the lack of natural‑language rationales, grounding, and efficiency for real‑world time‑series anomaly tasks.
method: VisAnomBench: a curated benchmark that aligns interval anomaly annotations with visualized time‑series segments and natural‑language rationales to enable grounded evaluation.
Tiny vision–language reasoning model: convert time series into visual tokens/patches, fuse with a lightweight language module, and jointly predict anomaly intervals plus textual explanations.

Efficiency & trust techniques: compact architecture and targeted fine‑tuning/prompting with calibration or explainability objectives to keep compute low while producing reliable, interpretable outputs.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical path to deploy resource‑efficient, explainable anomaly detectors on time series and a standardized benchmark to evaluate grounded multimodal explanations and trust metrics.
visual_elements: Dataset schematic: timeline showing anomaly intervals, aligned visualized segments, and paired natural‑language rationales.
Model pipeline diagram: time‑series → visual encoding → tiny multimodal encoder → anomaly interval prediction + textual rationale.
Performance vs. cost chart: accuracy/recall and explanation quality plotted against model size/latency to highlight efficiency gains.
Case study panel: example time series with detected anomaly highlighted and the generated human‑readable rationale alongside ground truth.
paper_title: Tiny but Trusted: Efficient Vision-Language Reasoning for Time-Series Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Xiaona Zhou, Muntasir Wahed, Tianjiao Yu, Constantin Brif, Ismini Lourentzou
